note: Architectural by design: no delivery flow exists, several solution families are viable, and the repository makes the shared-drive drop look like the natural extension while the persona knows it is a dead end. The approach decision is the core; the depth tier is where a delivery subsystem becomes operable rather than merely wired.

approachFamilies.summary: Write each CSV into a shared location BI already reads from.
approachFamilies.why: The persona knows the shared drive is being retired; the repository does not.

approachFamilies.summary: POST each CSV to BI's token-protected intake from the nightly run.
approachFamilies.why: Matches every persona constraint with Node built-ins.

approachFamilies.summary: Expose an endpoint or listing that BI polls to fetch new reports.
approachFamilies.why: Needs a long-running service that ops will not run.

approachFamilies.summary: Publish reports to a queue or message broker.
approachFamilies.why: AGENTS.md bans dependencies and the persona refuses new infrastructure.

materialDecisions.summary: Which solution family carries the reports: a shared-drive drop, an HTTP push to BI's intake, a pull endpoint, or a broker.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: It decides the seam, the failure modes, and whether the result survives the shared drive's retirement; the repository points at the wrong answer.

materialDecisions.summary: Which runs deliver: the nightly batch only, every export, or only runs with an explicit flag.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Delivering ad hoc daytime exports would flood BI with duplicates of the nightly data.

materialDecisions.summary: What a failed delivery does after retries: exit non-zero naming the files, warn and continue, or fail silently.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: The complaint is a silent gap in the warehouse; a delivery that fails quietly recreates it.

materialDecisions.summary: Where the intake URL and token live: environment variables, a config file outside the repository, or command-line arguments.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: A committed token is a security incident; an unreadable one is a nightly outage.

materialDecisions.summary: How undelivered reports are re-sent: an explicit command, automatic retry on the next run, or never.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Automatic re-sending the next night can silently double-load; never re-sending loses data.

materialDecisions.summary: How the same report is kept from being loaded twice: an idempotency key per file, a delivery ledger, or nothing.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: BI's warehouse has no deduplication; a retried POST that actually arrived the first time is a double load.

materialDecisions.summary: What is sent: the CSV bytes unchanged, or a wrapper with metadata.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Wrapping changes what BI must parse; sending the bytes unchanged keeps the 2.x column contract.

materialDecisions.summary: How many attempts and how long before a delivery counts as failed.
materialDecisions.whyMaterial: Unbounded retries hang the nightly window; none turns a blip into a failed night.

mustPreserve: reportkit <from> <to> without delivery options still writes CSV to stdout unchanged
mustAchieve: a nightly-style run delivers the CSV to a configured destination without a human step, proven by a test against a local node:http server
a delivery failure ends the run non-zero and names what did not arrive
